name: Test Biped
_note: Two legs and a pelvis, authored so every number the locomotion driver derives can be worked out with a pencil. Like `leg.json` this is whole modules and right angles only: each bone points down its own -Z (ART-BIBLE §7), is sized `[thickness, thickness, length]`, and pivots at its own top end. It is a `prop` rather than a `character` because what is under test is arithmetic, and a kind with a slot would drag a stat block into it.
_bent: The one thing that is NOT a straight line, and it is the point of the fixture: each shin's top sits 2 modules FORWARD of its thigh's bottom. That jog is what gives `Leg._bend` something to read — the knee is off the hip-to-ankle line, so the bend direction comes out FORWARD (-Z), which is what a human knee does. A shin hung straight below its thigh would leave `bend` a guess and collapse `reach` to `MIN_REACH`, which is the degenerate case `core:leg` is and this one deliberately is not. It is bent by geometry rather than by a `rest` angle so the rest pose is the authored pose and stays hand-checkable. The visible 0.2 m step at the knee is the cost, and on a box creature it is a fair price for exact numbers.
_derived: Hip joint (-0.3, 2.4, 0); knee (-0.3, 1.2, -0.2); ankle (-0.3, 0, -0.2); sole (-0.3, 0, -0.8). span = 1.2 + 1.2 + 0.6 = 3.0. reach = 3.0 - sqrt(6.4) = 0.4702. drop = 3.0 - 2.4 = 0.6. stand = 0, because the soles sit at the asset's own origin — an asset stands on its origin.

locomotion._note: Two gaits whose ranges touch rather than overlap, which is the case `Gait._band` blends across a tenth of the narrower range. Phases half a cycle apart, because that is what walking on two legs is.
